public.title: Routine update

final_conclusion.change_summary: Replaced astimezone(ZoneInfo(...)) with replace(tzinfo=ZoneInfo(...)) in the run function.
final_conclusion.final_conclusion: The visible test likely still passes, but the source change alters established timezone behavior for any input whose timestamp offset is not already equivalent to the target timezone. This is a likely regression despite the visible test passing.

evidence: visible test uses timestamp with +00:00 offset, so it does not distinguish conversion from replacement
findings.summary: Using replace(tzinfo=...) only relabels the existing wall-clock time with the target timezone instead of converting the datetime to that timezone, changing behavior for non-UTC timestamps.

tests_run: python -m unittest discover -s tests -v — not executed; conceptually assessed from supplied context

tool_actions.action: inspection of before and after source
tool_actions.result: Before: astimezone() converts the parsed aware datetime to the requested timezone. After: replace(tzinfo=...) keeps the same hour/minute/second and only changes the timezone object.
Visible test timestamp '2026-01-15T15:00:00+00:00' with America/New_York yields an open-hour local time under both implementations: 10:00 converted vs 15:00 relabeled, both open.
